thread.title_full: ValleyCats tie playoff series on Campos' walk-off homer - NewsBreak

author: Mark Singelais
title: ValleyCats tie playoff series on Campos' walk-off homer - NewsBreak
text:
By Mark Singelais ,
1 hours ago Tri-City ValleyCats catcher Oscar Campos, shown earlier in the playoffs against Sussex County, hit a walk-off homer in the bottom of the ninth to beat Quebec in Game 2 of the Frontier League's Atlantic Conference Finals on Wednesday at Bruno Stadium. (Jim Franco/Times Union) TROY — Fan favorite Oscar Campos gave the Tri-City home crowd another reason to love him on Wednesday night with a hit that gave the ValleyCats a crucial postseason victory.
Campos' two-out, solo homer in the bottom of the ninth lifted the ValleyCats to a 7-6 win over the Quebec Capitales in Game 2 of the Frontier League’s Atlantic Conference Finals before 1,605 fans at Joseph L. Bruno Stadium.
The blast tied the best-of-5 series at 1-1 heading to Stade Canac in Quebec City for Game 3 on Friday, Game 4 on Saturday and, if necessary, Game 5 on Sunday.
“It’s a pretty exciting moment,” Campos said. “It was the first time in my whole career that I hit a walk-off homer and, honestly, it feels amazing.”
After teammates mobbed him and poured a Gatorade bucket on him at home plate, fans showered Campos with chants of “Oscar, Oscar,” in what could have been Tri-City’s final home game of the season. He’s the longest-tenured player in franchise history in his fifth season with the team.
“It was a moment for him that I know he’ll remember for the rest of his life, I’m sure,” ValleyCats manager Greg Tagert said.
Campos, a catcher and designated hitter, played on the 2018 team that won the New York-Penn League when the ValleyCats were still a Houston Astros affiliate. He has spent another four seasons with Tri-City in the independent Frontier League. He missed a month earlier this season after having an appendectomy.
On Wednesday, Campos crushed a first-pitch curveball from Quebec reliever Emile Boies well beyond the left-field fence.
Boies struck out Josue Urdaneta and Chris Burgess to begin the inning, and Campos noticed Boies had started both of those batters off with fastballs for called strikes.
“I went to home plate thinking as a catcher,” Campos said. “I told myself, 'OK, he’s not going to throw me a fastball. He doesn’t want me to do some damage to the fastball. He’s going to throw me a curveball because, the whole game, they’ve been throwing me curveballs.'”
The victory kept the ValleyCats from falling into a 0-2 series hole and needing a three-game sweep at three-time defending league champion Quebec this weekend. Now Tri-City must win two of three.
“It makes that bus ride much more enjoyable tomorrow, let me tell you, and gives us a chance to know we’ve got at least two more games in Quebec,” Tagert said. “It’s going to be a challenging place, but a great place for our guys. That’s one thing about this ballclub, those moments aren’t going to be too big for them.”
ValleyCats outfielder Demias Jimerson, put in the lineup for Game 2, hit a two-run double to left to tie the score at 4-4 in the third inning. Then, Jimerson scored on a throwing error by Quebec third baseman Kendall Simmons for a 5-4 lead.
Tri-City tacked on an insurance run on David Glancy’s RBI double to left that made it 6-4 in the sixth inning.
Meanwhile, ValleyCats starting pitcher Connor Wilford retired the final 11 batters he faced and lasted through six innings.
But Tri-City reliever Jalon Long allowed a two-run homer to left by Quebec’s Kyle Crowl to knot the score at 6-6 in the eighth inning.
“Then you get a little ValleyCats magic there with the right guy (Campos) that seems to be somewhat popular here,” Tagert said.
